subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should reset archive recovery be solved through read-only family history only, a Doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: The choice changes whether OpenClaw mutates archived transcripts and session indexes, how it exposes private prior context, and how retained/pruned reset archives are represented to users, so automation should not pick the permanent recovery boundary.

options.title: Land read-only family history first
options.body: Use an explicit, bounded family-history selector as the supported retrieval path before adding any archive-to-active mutation.

options.title: Add Doctor-owned restore/re-index
options.body: Create a deliberate recovery command for affected users that preserves source metadata and explains retention and security consequences.

options.title: Reject mutation-style restore
options.body: Keep reset archives read-only and track only discovery, export, and history-reading surfaces.

recommendation.title: Land read-only family history first
recommendation.body: Use an explicit, bounded family-history selector as the supported retrieval path before adding any archive-to-active mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame routes the central session-history and archive-discovery lines through this recent area commit, though product direction likely needs broader owner review.
